doc.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: John Levy, Nancy Wilson and the rhythm section
summary: Nancy Wilson wants to tour with the band, and Kay talks about John Levy and rhythm section life.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So it’s Nancy Wilson. And I know John. See John played with George Shearing when I was with Patti Page. We played the Chicago Theater together. So I know John a long time. John is a good bass player. And so we talked. And I said, “hey John, listen, if the rhythm gets tired you and I will play. You get your bass, I’ll get the drums.” I said, “it’s be like a dirge, like a funeral in New Orleans.” And John told me something funny, John would say, “yeah.” He said, “imagine the rhythm section and we’re out there playing and there’s eight people in front and we’re playing eighty choruses and they said to John and ‘you’ve got it.’” And John says, “got what?” He can’t play anymore like they do. You know the rhythm section, like they get all — the brunt is on them. Everybody, four choruses they go and they go for a drink and [scats].
I always feel sorry for them.
Yeah the rhythm section, we get it. Just keep playing, they don’t care. So but we’ve had a lot of fun.
